title: Platform Admin Ops Triage — RBAC, Cost, On-call Handoff

Agreed next steps: draft runbook edits, deploy RBAC audit query, schedule dry-run key rotation window, and assign cost tag owners for the upcoming billing cycle.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~65 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Janelle, Samir, Lina, Priya, Tom, Evan

Summary / Purpose: quick triage across IT / FinOps / Security to close gaps before end-of-quarter billing run and KMS rotation window.

[00:00] Aisha Patel: Alright everyone we can get started, thank you for hopping on. I know this is tight before the holiday push so we'll try to keep it focused.

[00:15] Samir Choudhury: Thanks Aisha. Main things from FinOps: we saw some unexpected tagging gaps in Dedicated clusters and a handful of untagged endpoints spiking last billing period, wants to avoid surprises this cycle.

[00:38] Marco Ruiz: Got it. Are those mostly customer-initiated dedicated pools or internal test clusters?

[00:43] Samir Choudhury: A mix — about 60% customer, 40% internal. The internal ones are where we can move fastest to remediate.

[01:05] Lina Gomez: On the IT side, we have a pending KMS rotation the security team flagged. Need to coordinate a dry run because some on-prem connectors have tight windows.

[01:25] Priya Nair: Yes. The security ask is Rotate keys mid-December ideally, but before rotating we need an audit of services using those keys. We don't want to break Dedicated brokers or any on-prem control-plane endpoints.

[01:47] Janelle King: Also, the on-call rotation swap is next week. I want to verify handoff steps so whoever is on-call knows where to look for RBAC issues and cost alerts. Last time there was confusion about escalation to Platform.

[02:10] Tom Blevins: Echoing that. We need clearer ownership for 'privileged alert' for infra-control-plane. Sometimes PagerDuty routing goes to infra-systems and sometimes to app platform.

[02:35] Aisha Patel: Ok so today's goals: 1) agree owner and timeline for RBAC audit, 2) confirm KMS rotation dry-run owner and window, 3) finalize simple cost-tagging list and owners, 4) update on-call runbook items. Anything missing?

[03:00] Evan Li: Quick note from finance intern — a couple of cost centers don't map cleanly to product teams, Samir asked me to flag those for the mapping doc.

[03:15] Samir Choudhury: Yep thanks Evan. I'll review the mapping doc after this.

[03:30] Marco Ruiz: For RBAC audit I'll propose a query set: list of principals with roles containing 'admin', 'owner', 'full_access', plus service accounts older than 90 days. That should capture the bulk. But beware false positives like cross-account roles for SRE-runbooks.

[03:55] Priya Nair: And include keys attached to those principals — if a service account has active key material and admin perms that's priority.

[04:12] Janelle King: Marco, can you also include last-used timestamp? We had a case where a service account looked active but hadn't been used in months.

[04:28] Marco Ruiz: Yeah we can add last-used. I'll try to produce an export CSV. Might need to run as a slightly privileged query so I'll coordinate with Lina for temporary access.

[04:45] Lina Gomez: I'll grant a scoped role to Marco for the audit window, logging that as part of the process.

[05:05] Aisha Patel: Great. On the cost tagging side — Samir, what's the minimal set that would buy us good accuracy without overburdening teams?

[05:20] Samir Choudhury: Minimal set: product_team, environment (prod/stage/dev), billing_project, model_family, committed_customer_id. If we can get those on Dedicated pools we can roll up spend by customer and model family.

[05:42] Tom Blevins: For model_family tag, we need to standardize values — e.g., gpt-like, llama-like, redwood-verified. Otherwise rollups won't group properly.

[06:05] Priya Nair: Security needs a separate tag for data-sensitivity classification for private deployments. It can't be freeform.

[06:22] Janelle King: Ok so we have two streams: production-facing tags for billing, and sensitivity tag for compliance. We'll produce a short doc with allowed values. Tom you volunteer to draft the mapping?

[06:40] Tom Blevins: I'll draft it and include examples.

[07:00] Marco Ruiz: Back to KMS rotation — what's our tolerance window? How long can we afford a degraded state during rotation?

[07:15] Priya Nair: Ideally zero downtime, but realistically we should plan for a short window: 15-30 minutes for any connector that requires re-keying. We'll document rollback steps.

[07:35] Samir Choudhury: From billing side, rotation mid-December is fine as long as we run a dry-run with a non-prod Dedicated pool before hitting prod.

[07:50] Lina Gomez: We should test on the staging control-plane first, then a small subset of Dedicated customer pools that can tolerate the window. We have two customers who volunteered as canaries.

[08:05] Aisha Patel: Who will own the dry-run?

[08:12] Priya Nair: Security will lead the plan, Janelle will coordinate the on-call side, Lina will coordinate the environment prep, and Samir will validate billing signals post-dry-run.

[08:27] Janelle King: I'll add the dry-run timeline to the runbook and include contact points and rollback.

[08:40] Evan Li: Should we notify customers of planned rotation? The canary customers probably want a heads up.

[08:50] Tom Blevins: Yes short notification plus 'no expected impact' caveat. For full prod rotation we'll schedule a maintenance window.

[09:05] Marco Ruiz: Regarding RBAC cleanup — a process question: do we remove roles immediately or create a review ticket and temporarily remove privileges?

[09:20] Priya Nair: Security prefers to remove or reduce scope for stale service accounts after review. For human accounts we should require approval via ticket. For service accounts older than 90 days and unused, auto-flag and then remove after 7 days if no claims.

[09:40] Samir Choudhury: Sounds reasonable. Cost tagging: if we enforce tags, who auto-applies for missed cases? We can use a default tag for untagged resources to surface them in reports.

[09:55] Tom Blevins: We have a lambda that can apply a 'untagged' marker but it requires review because it can skew chargebacks. Maybe better to alert owners and Comptroller to reconcile.

[10:10] Janelle King: For on-call handoff, two changes: 1) add 'cost surge' runbook link to the top of the on-call doc, 2) add a quick RBAC triage checklist (query, who to escalate to).

[10:28] Marco Ruiz: I'll write the sample RBAC triage query and send it to Janelle.

[10:40] Aisha Patel: Good. Any blockers or open risks?

[10:45] Priya Nair: Potential blocker: some older Dedicated orchestration nodes are tied to a legacy KMS alias that isn't in our automation. We need to ensure rotation won't orphan them. That requires a short inventory sweep.

[11:05] Lina Gomez: I'll run inventory on the legacy aliases and produce a list. Could take 48 hours but I'll prioritize.

[11:25] Tom Blevins: Also we still have a backlog of stale IAM policies in the infra repo. Cleaning them up will reduce noise in the RBAC audit. We should plan a small sprint.

[11:40] Aisha Patel: Ok Tom, add that to your deliverables.

[11:50] Evan Li: Small ask — can we add a billing tag 'pilot-owner-email' so we can reach the right contact quickly for canaries?

[12:00] Samir Choudhury: Good idea. Add to the mapping doc as optional but recommended.

[12:15] Marco Ruiz: I'm worried about access levels for the audit — if I grant myself the scope I might have elevated logs. We'll make sure it's temporary and logged.

[12:35] Lina Gomez: All temporary grants will be done through the access-request workflow and we'll note them in the ticket.

[12:50] Priya Nair: For KMS rotation contingency: plan to skip a node and replicate if it fails. We'll add that to the dry-run plan.

[13:10] Janelle King: I'll circulate the updated runbook draft; please provide comments inline within 48 hours.

[13:25] Aisha Patel: Recap then: Marco runs RBAC audit (due 11-20), Janelle updates runbook and adds cost surge and RBAC triage (due 11-22), Tom drafts tag mapping and addresses stale IAM policies (mapping due 11-21, stale cleanup backlog start 11-23), Priya + Lina lead KMS dry-run plan (due 11-24), Samir validates tag set and billing labels (due 11-21).

[13:55] Tom Blevins: Quick note — I'll also open a short PR to standardize model_family values, will include examples.

[14:10] Samir Choudhury: After tasks complete we'll run the billing report and check for untagged spend before closing the loop.

[14:25] Aisha Patel: Perfect. Anything else?

[14:33] Evan Li: No, thanks all.

[14:36] Marco Ruiz: Thanks everyone.

[14:45] Meeting end.

Referenced artifacts/links:
